title: Singapore's FATF mutual evaluation: beneficial ownership, legal assistance and asset recovery
asked: Mr Chua asked how the Government will address gaps in verification requirements and the accuracy of beneficial ownership information, and what steps it will take to reduce delays in mutual legal assistance requests, increase the use of formal and informal cooperation channels in transnational crime investigations, and speed up asset recovery from abroad.
response: Mr Murali Pillai said Singapore was placed on regular follow-up, the FATF category for countries assessed to have performed well, and that the Government will study the FATF's recommendations and develop risk-proportionate action plans. He said straightforward mutual legal assistance requests are executed in as little as three days and complex ones in about 10 weeks, and set out the beneficial ownership regime: a central registry for companies and LLPs, periodic verification, customer due diligence by banks, and checks by the Singapore Land Authority on landed residential property buyers. Maximum financial penalties on financial institutions and virtual asset service providers rose from $800,000 in the previous evaluation to $5.8 million this round. On the supplementary on beneficial ownership, he said law enforcement agencies can and have obtained timely, accurate information on unregistered foreign companies and legal arrangements.

key_points.point: Singapore was placed on regular follow-up, the FATF category for countries assessed to have performed well.
key_points.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
key_points.quote: the FATF has placed Singapore on regular follow-up, which is the category for countries that have been assessed to have performed well

key_points.point: Straightforward mutual legal assistance requests are executed in as little as three days; complex ones take about 10 weeks on average.
key_points.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
key_points.quote: Straightforward requests are executed in as little as three days, while complex requests are executed within an average of about 10 weeks.

key_points.point: There is a central beneficial ownership registry for all companies and Limited Liability Partnerships, with periodic verification required.
key_points.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
key_points.quote: we have a central BO registry for all companies and Limited Liability Partnerships

key_points.point: For landed residential properties, the Singapore Land Authority checks the identity and citizenship of the ultimate beneficial owner.
key_points.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
key_points.quote: for landed residential properties, the Singapore Land Authority will conduct checks on the identity and the citizenship of the ultimate beneficial owner

key_points.point: Maximum financial penalties on financial institutions and virtual asset service providers rose from $800,000 in the previous evaluation to $5.8 million this round.
key_points.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
key_points.quote: the maximum financial penalties imposed on FIs and VASPs increased from $800,000 in the previous ME to $5.8 million this round

key_points.point: On the FATF recommendation to review the dissuasiveness and proportionality of financial penalties, the Government will consider it case by case.
key_points.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
key_points.quote: We will consider the recommendation, bearing in mind the specific details of each individual case and the range of enforcement levers available.

key_points.point: Law enforcement agencies can and have obtained timely, accurate beneficial ownership information on unregistered foreign companies and legal arrangements.
key_points.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
key_points.quote: there was no evidence that the BO information was inaccurate

key_points.point: Singapore will continue to issue mutual legal assistance requests where appropriate and also pursue informal international cooperation, including for scams.
key_points.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
key_points.quote: Singapore will continue to issue MLAs where it is appropriate, but also pursue international cooperation in informal manner.

key_points.point: Representative offices of foreign flag states in Singapore are subject to and must comply with Singapore's laws, including UN Security Council sanctions.
key_points.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
key_points.quote: these offices are subject to and must comply with Singapore's laws

left_open: Whether the central beneficial ownership register's coverage will be extended to Variable Capital Companies and unregistered foreign companies, and any timeline for doing so.
Specific steps to increase the number of mutual legal assistance requests Singapore sends abroad, including for scam-related asset recovery.
supplementary: Supplementary questions covered beneficial ownership register coverage, use of mutual legal assistance and asset recovery, and proliferation financing risks in the maritime sector.
